editorial.headline: KBLI 46441: The Wholesale Trade Behind Human Pharmaceutical Supply
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the wholesale distribution of pharmaceutical preparations for human use, open across every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46441 concerns the wholesale trade of pharmaceutical preparations intended for human use. Its scope is deliberately broad: medicinal ingredients, natural medicinal ingredients, cosmetics, quasi-drugs, health supplements, medicines and natural medicines all sit within the activity when their intended use is human. In practical terms, this is a wholesale-trade classification for the movement of these preparations through the supply chain, rather than a narrow category confined to one product form.

The record identifies both Pharmaceutical Wholesalers and Pharmaceutical Wholesaler Branches within that scope. It is open to enterprises operating at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, so the classification is not reserved for a single size of business. That breadth matters because the activity describes a commercial function—the wholesale trade of the listed preparations—while allowing that function to be carried out across the full range of recorded enterprise scales.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear: the activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A foreign investor may therefore hold the full permitted stake under the national position recorded for this code. The reference basis given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That is the national picture, and it should be read plainly: there is no lower foreign-ownership cap in this record.

Bali also remains open for PMA registration under the recorded local assessment. The province’s permanent moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA island-wide, but this activity is not blocked by that rule. At Besar scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why it falls outside the moratorium’s stated reach. For a foreign-owned business considering this wholesale activity in Bali, the honest conclusion is straightforward: the national 100% ceiling applies, and the Bali record does not show a moratorium block.
